topic: EARN: a 20-minute Asked-For List made by scrolling one month of text messages to spot skills people already ask you for, then writing one plain sentence offer
pillar: EARN: small, realistic ways to bring money in or make a skill pay, with no promises about amounts.
caption:
Your phone already knows what you are good at. 📱

Scroll back one month in your texts and write down every time someone asked you for help.
Circle the task you liked doing most.
Then write one plain sentence about it, like: I can help with resume edits on weekday evenings.
That sentence is a small start, and it is yours to change.

Save this for a quiet twenty minutes this week.

Want a place to write your Three Numbers next to it? The free Three Numbers Starter Sheet is a one-page worksheet, link in bio.

Day one counts.

General education, not financial advice.

slides.title: What do people already ask you for?
slides.subtitle: A 20-minute EARN step on your phone

slides.title: Start with your text messages
slides.body: People tend to ask you for help with the things you do well. Your phone keeps a record of it. This takes about twenty minutes and a notes app or one sheet of paper.

slides.title: Make your Asked-For List
items: Open your texts and scroll back about one month
Write down each time someone asked you for help
Use plain words, like fixed my resume
Put a check next to anything asked more than once
Circle the one you liked doing most

slides.title: Small asks belong on the list
slides.body: Editing a cover letter counts. So does watching a dog for a weekend or sorting out a messy spreadsheet. If someone asked, write it down.

slides.title: Write one plain sentence
slides.body: Take your circled task and turn it into a line. Example: I can help with resume edits on weekday evenings. That is a draft. You can change it any time.

slides.title: Where this fits
slides.body: Any money this brings in goes in your first number, what is coming in. Side income can affect taxes, so a licensed tax professional can help with the details.

slides.title: Keep your list next to your numbers
slides.body: Save this post for a quiet twenty minutes. The free Three Numbers Starter Sheet is a one-page worksheet in my Stan store, link in bio. Day one counts.
